flawed_step: Lines 0014–0018 incorrectly treat 10 log m as O(m^{-0.5}); the displayed limit only shows log m=o(m^{0.5}). Consequently, the cited Master-theorem case does not apply.
counterexample: Take logarithms base 2 and set S(1)=0. For m=2^k, the recurrence gives S(2^k)=S(2^{k-1})+10k, so S(1)=0, S(2)=10, S(4)=30, S(8)=60, and generally S(2^k)=10(1+2+...+k)=5k(k+1). This is unbounded, directly contradicting the claimed S(m)=Theta(1).
assessment_summary: The proof's key asymptotic comparison reverses the relevant power: log m grows more slowly than m^{0.5}, but it is not bounded by the decaying function m^{-0.5}. Unrolling the recurrence on powers of two yields Theta((log m)^2), not Theta(1).
